title: Philippines, Japan sign emergency loan, water supply grant deals
summary: The Philippines and Japan have signed two landmark deals that will allow loans and grants to help boost the Philippine economy and improve water supply systems in Cotabato City.

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The Philippines and Japan have signed two landmark deals that will allow loans and grants to help boost the Philippine economy and improve water supply systems in Cotabato City.
Both deals are expected to benefit the Philippines amid current economic challenges and water supply problems in the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (BARMM).

The Japanese embassy in Manila announced yesterday that Ambassador Kitagawa Katsuro and Foreign Affairs Secretary Ma. Theresa Lazaro signed and exchanged notes for the “Emergency Support Loan for Enhancing Economic Resilience and Poverty Alleviation” on Nov. 13 with a loan limit of approximately 70 billion yen.

“With its reliance on the Middle East for approximately 95 percent of its crude oil and petroleum products, the Philippines is significantly affected by increasing energy and raw material prices and supply chain instability stemming from the situation in the Middle East,” the embassy said.
“Rising production costs and logistical bottlenecks are posing challenges to the stable supply of products that underpin Japan’s supply chains.”

The Japanese embassy noted that under the “POWERR Asia” initiative launched by Japan, its support will bolster emergency economic measures, such as stabilizing energy supply to mitigate the impact of the situation in the Middle East and addressing soaring prices, thereby stabilizing and strengthening supply chains throughout Asia.
At the same time, such initiatives will also contribute to Japan’s economic security and benefit Japanese companies operating in the region.

Earlier on Nov. 9, Kitagawa and Lazaro also signed and exchanged notes for a project aimed to improve the water supply system in Cotabato City with a maximum grant amount of approximately 3.644 billion yen.

The embassy said the project will expand water supply facilities in Cotabato City, the capital of BARMM where socio-economic development has lagged due to prolonged conflict and limited access to safe water.
“By expanding safe water supply services, this cooperation will contribute to the consolidation of peace and development in Mindanao through the reduction of disparities.”
